title: Unified Request-to-Provision: Access, Change, Data & Procurement Workflow
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Summary:
This document defines the single, company-wide Request-to-Provision workflow used by Redwood Inference teams for: access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor onboarding, travel approvals, and the canonical internal templates used to collect requests. The goal is to standardize approvals, reduce time-to-provision, and ensure compliance with security and finance controls.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: All employees, contractors, and third-party vendors requesting access to systems, purchasing goods/services, requesting change windows, or provisioning data resources.
- Intent: Provide a single flow with clear decision criteria, owners, SLAs, and templates. Avoid ad-hoc email approvals and reduce duplicate reviews.

Quick flow (text diagram):
1) Request creation (ServiceNow/Confluence form or Slack /ops bot) -> 2) Automated triage (risk classification) -> 3) Approval chain (based on risk and cost) -> 4) Provisioning / PO / Change execution -> 5) Audit & closure (logs + retrospective)

Definitions:
- Low-risk: Standard employee access, budget < $1,000, non-production read-only data.
- Medium-risk: Elevated privileges, budget $1,000–$50,000, production non-PII data writes.
- High-risk: Admin/sysadmin roles, budget > $50,000, production PII or regulated data or vendor-managed infra.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Requester: Completes form with purpose, business justification, expiry, and risk inputs.
- Request Triage (Automation + Oncall): ServiceNow intake + automated risk scoring.
- Approvers: Manager -> Security -> Finance -> Legal (escalate depending on risk/cost).
- Provisioning Owner: System owner or EngOps executes the change/provision and marks complete.
- Audit Owner: Compliance team ensures logs and evidence stored.

Approval matrix (table):
| Request Type | Low-risk approver | Medium-risk approver | High-risk approver | Notes |
|--------------|-------------------|----------------------|--------------------|-------|
| Access (non-admin) | Manager | Manager + Security | Manager + Security + IT Head | Auto-expire 90 days unless renewed |
| Admin role | Manager + Security | Security + Eng Lead | Security + Eng Head + Legal | Multi-factor + training required |
| Procurement | Requester Manager | Finance | Finance + Legal | PO required over $5k |
| Vendor onboarding | N/A | Security + Procurement | Security + Legal + Procurement Head | Security assessment required |

SLA targets and metrics:
- Low-risk requests: 98% fulfilled within 4 business hours.
- Medium-risk requests: 95% fulfilled within 48 business hours.
- High-risk requests: 90% reviewed and scheduled within 5 business days.
- Audit evidence retention: 3 years for standard logs; 7 years for contract & legal evidence where required.

Detailed procedure: step-by-step
1) Request creation (templates)
   - Requester fills the canonical request template (see Templates section). Required fields: requester, team, justification, requested resources, expiry date, business impact, cost estimate, data classification.
   - Channels: Primary intake is ServiceNow form; Slack /ops-bot for low-risk self-service; email only for exceptional cases (must be converted to ServiceNow ticket within 24h).
2) Automated triage
   - System scores risk based on resource type, data classification, and cost. Rules: any request referencing PII, regulated datasets, or budget > $50k is High-risk.
   - Create triage tags: low/medium/high and append to ticket.
3) Approval chain
   - Low-risk: auto-route to manager for approval. If manager approves, provisioning runs via self-service playbook.
   - Medium-risk: manager -> security (30 business hour SLA) -> provisioning owner.
   - High-risk: manager + security + finance/legal review. Schedule change window where required.
4) Provisioning and change control
   - Provisioning owner follows the runbook for the target service. Record start/end time, operator, and all commands in change log.
   - For changes impacting production, use the change calendar and notify stakeholders via the runbook channels.
   - Emergency changes: follow Emergency Change process (appendix) with post-facto CAB review within 48 hours.
5) Verification and closure
   - Requester verifies access/purchase. Provisioning owner marks ticket done and attaches verification evidence.
   - Compliance team performs random quarterly audits (10% sample) and escalates exceptions.

Change management specifics:
- Standard change window: Mon–Fri 02:00–05:00 UTC for non-critical infra.
- Maintenance blackout window: major product release periods; check calendar before scheduling.
- CAB (Change Advisory Board): weekly, chaired by EngOps, includes Security, SRE, Product, and a Finance delegate.
- Emergency change path: documented template; requires at least two oncall approvals and a written post-change justification.

Data classification & handling:
- Classification levels: PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED.
- Storage requirements:
   - PUBLIC: no special controls.
   - INTERNAL: encrypted at rest; role-based access.
   - CONFIDENTIAL: encryption at rest and in transit; access limited to explicit approvals and logged actions.
   - RESTRICTED (PII, regulated): KMS-backed encryption, HSM for keys if required; SIEM alerting on exfiltration events.
- Data provisioning checklist (must be attached to request): justification, retention policy, access list, masking/encryption plan, and deletion schedule.

Procurement and expenses rules:
- Expense thresholds and approvals:
   - <$1,000: Manager approval, expense report via Expensify.
   - $1,000–$5,000: Manager + Finance review.
   - $5,000–$50,000: Finance approval + PO.
   - >$50,000: Finance + Legal + Executive sponsorship.
- Vendor onboarding steps:
   1. Fill Vendor Intake form.
   2. Procurement performs vendor risk assessment (security, financial, sanctions).
   3. Security performs technical assessment (penetration, data handling).
   4. Legal reviews contract and SLAs.
   5. Procurement issues PO and adds vendor to approved vendor registry.
- Payment terms: Standard net-30 unless negotiated. Invoices must route to AP queue with PO reference.

Travel and hospitality (summary):
- Booking: Employees should use the corporate travel tool for flights and hotels. Personal bookings require pre-approval.
- Approval thresholds: Domestic travel: manager approval; international travel: manager + People Ops; travel with third-party vendor: manager + Legal review if contract involvement.
- Per diem and expenses: follow the company expense policy template; receipts required for amounts > $25.

Templates (canonical forms):
- Access request (access-request-template.yml):
  ```yaml
  requester: name@example.com
  team: Platform Engineering
  resource: redwood-prod-s3-bucket
  access_level: read-only
  justification: "needed for daily reconciliation job"
  expiry: 2025-05-01
  data_classification: INTERNAL
  cost_center: ENG-PLATFORM
  ```
- Procurement request (procurement-request-template.md): includes budget code, vendor, justification, PO_needed boolean.
- Emergency change template (emergency-change.md): fields for timeline, risk, mitigations, and rollback plan.

Example automation snippet (ServiceNow rule):
- Condition: if cost > 50000 OR data_classification in [RESTRICTED] => assign to security@redwood.com and procurement@redwood.com; set priority HIGH.

Audit and evidence storage:
- All approvals, signed contracts, and change logs must be stored in the GCP-backed evidence bucket (path: gs://redwood-audit/evidence/<year>/).
- Retention: 3 years for routine access; escalate retention to legal if contract requires longer.

Escalation paths:
- 24h overdue medium request: auto-notify manager and EngOps.
- 72h overdue high request: page Security Lead and Finance Director.
- SLA breach reporting: weekly digest to Ops Leadership with ticket IDs and remediation actions.

Operational tooling and automation recommendations:
- Integrate Okta groups with ServiceNow auto-provisioning for low-risk requests.
- Use signed attestations for admin role requests (training confirmation).
- Enforce short-lived credentials for third-party vendor sessions.

Appendices:
A) Emergency change checklist (one-page): include rollback commands, contact list, and postmortem template.
B) Sample approval email subject lines and templates for Finance and Legal review.
C) Template IDs:
   - ACCESS_REQ_V1 (access-request-template.yml)
   - PROCUREMENT_REQ_V2 (procurement-request-template.md)
   - EMER_CHANGE_V1 (emergency-change.md)

Owners and contact list:
- Workflow owner: Finance Ops (workflow-owner@redwood.com)
- Security intake: security@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Compliance & Audit: compliance@redwood.com
